name: Jobab
overview: Jobab was a male king known as the King of Madon. He is noted in Scripture as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. His role as a ruler places him among the Canaanite kings opposing Israel's entrance into the Promised Land.
namesAndTitles: The name Jobab means 'howl' in Hebrew, reflecting its original linguistic form. Additionally, he is identified by the title 'King of Madon,' which simply denotes his rulership over the city of Madon. Neither his personal name nor his title is described as given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Jobab beyond his kingship of Madon. There are no genealogical details or relational connections provided in the biblical text concerning him.
scriptureSignificance: Jobab's significance lies in his inclusion among the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua, marking the fulfillment of God's promise to give Israel the land of Canaan. His defeat symbolizes the overthrow of Canaanite authority and the establishment of Israelite dominion under God's guidance. As King of Madon, Jobab represents the local opposition to God's chosen people during this pivotal period.
